$comment: Claims about this repository that were asserted and PROVEN FALSE. An AI contributor starts every session with no memory of the last one, so the same wrong claim can be made indefinitely. This file is that memory, made mechanical. Enforced by scripts/check-known-false-claims.mjs, which re-verifies every refutation against the tree AND fails if any tracked document re-states one. Never delete an entry to make the gate pass: if the tree genuinely changed, update the entry deliberately and say so, or the lesson is lost.

claims.claimed: Android does not exist in any form — zero .kt, .gradle or android files
claims.assertedBy: docs/DELIVERY_GAP_ANALYSIS.md, then repeated by two external analyses
claims.whyItHappened: The document was measured correctly and then overtaken the same morning by PR #196. Everyone downstream quoted the document instead of the tree.

claims.claimed: No Electron, Tauri, .csproj or .sln files exist — there is no native desktop shell
claims.whyItHappened: Same stale-document error; native/desktop landed in PR #199 hours later.

claims.claimed: Embedded firmware is ABSENT — zero .ino, .c, .cpp or .h files in the entire repository
claims.whyItHappened: THE SEARCH WAS THE ERROR, not the tree. It enumerated C-family extensions only, so it could not have found the firmware whether or not it existed — the firmware is Rust. This is the exact failure absence-check.mjs exists to prevent: one pattern shape is not exhaustion.

claims.claimed: iOS is the only genuinely native platform
claims.assertedBy: docs/DELIVERY_GAP_ANALYSIS.md, then repeated by two external analyses
claims.whyItHappened: Inherited from the three absence errors above rather than measured on its own.

claims.claimed: The launch-profile scope decision is stranded on an unmerged branch — variously '7 files versus 2' and 'the branch is 220 commits ahead' — and merging it blocks everything else
claims.assertedBy: docs/DELIVERY_GAP_ANALYSIS.md, then two external analyses independently, as their #1 finding
claims.whyItHappened: PR #152 merged on 2026-08-12 (e11f2cc) and the document was never restamped. The numbers were never file counts: 7 was a commits-ahead count, 2 was a modified-file count, and 220 was invented outright — the branch was 8 ahead and 0 behind when it was written. THIS IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE ENTRY HERE: it survived two independent reviews because it was already shaped like a measurement.

claims.claimed: This repository has roughly 180 proof gates (elsewhere: 122)
claims.assertedBy: two external analyses, one high and one low
claims.whyItHappened: Neither analysis counted. The repo publishes the real figure in docs/STATUS.md and binds it with two gates (check-status-figures, check-proof-counts); both analyses quoted a remembered number instead, in documents whose whole argument was that this repo's discipline is measured figures. NOTE 2026-08-15: this entry originally pinned the literal count (132) as its refutation evidence, and broke the first time a proof was ADDED — the count is owned by the gates, so the registry now pins the MECHANISM (a gate-bound published figure exists) rather than any value of it.

claims.claimed: routeOwner does not exist anywhere in the codebase today (listed among five fields that are 'a design target')
claims.whyItHappened: A TRUE narrow claim was written as a BROAD one. The narrow claim — routeOwner is not a field on `Decision`, and the IT-layer model puts owner routing on no wire by design — is correct and still stands. It was generalised to 'does not exist anywhere in the codebase', which is false: owner routing ships as scripts/it-layer-model.mjs plus a console mirror that check-it-layer-model.mjs fails the build over in both directions. The other four fields in the same sentence genuinely appear nowhere, which is what made the fifth easy to wave through — a list is only as true as its weakest member, and nobody re-checks a member that arrived with four correct siblings.
denials: [Ff]ive of those fields do not exist anywhere

claims.claimed: The live-vendor proofs (Fleet, Keycloak, FreeRADIUS/RADIUS, Wazuh) each run in CI
claims.whyItHappened: The proofs are committed and were each run live once on the maintainer's Mac lane; a buyer-facing summary compressed 'committed proof, proven live on the lab' into 'runs in CI', which is stronger and false — the live-server proofs hard-exit without a provisioned server and no workflow provisions one. Only the in-process live-idp proof runs in CI.

refutation.$why: The live-fleet proof reads FLEET_URL from the environment and refuses without a provisioned server; no workflow in .github/workflows sets it, so it cannot run in CI. The deterministic proof:fleet-connector is a DIFFERENT proof that legitimately runs in CI — do not conflate them.

denials: each driven by a committed proof that runs in CI
